signal: Field Materials raised a $10.5M Series A to automate construction procurement; plans to triple revenue

email.body1:
Justin, saw Field Materials closed its $10.5M Series A to automate construction procurement, with plans to triple revenue this year.

Tripling revenue usually means far more in-market accounts than reps can touch, and hiring SDRs fast enough rarely keeps pace. Our AI SDR turns buying signals into booked meetings at 3-5x per rep, with no new headcount.

I built a signal play for Field Materials off your hiring and tech-stack signals, accounts showing those progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.subject2: where your reps lose selling time
email.body2:
Justin, following up on the revenue-tripling plan at Field Materials.

When targets jump, reps end up buried in research, writing, and CRM logging instead of selling, which quietly caps how many of those 8,000-plus vendor-side accounts you actually cover. The fix is output per rep, not more hires.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound, 3 things I'd change. Our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50-70%.
email.body3:
Justin, one proof point relevant to scaling Field Materials' pipeline.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than their team could touch. Using this, they booked $2.7M in qualified pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, with the same headcount. That's the kind of coverage tripling revenue demands.

Want to grab time so I can walk you through how Field Materials' reply rate compares to other Series A startups running outbound?
